stages.title: Resolve inputs

produces.label: render input manifest (counts + a SHA-256 fingerprint of the inputs)

stages.note: Reads what the project actually holds and fingerprints it. No file: this stage's output is the manifest recorded on its own stage row.

output.projectTitle: Real footage, one scene — a Pixabay clip encoded by this pipeline
output.fingerprintBasis: SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of {projectId, presetId, scenes[id,order,duration,narrationChars,sourcePath]}

progressAfterStage.arithmetic: 10% = (10) / 100 — weights of the 1 stage(s) that actually succeeded (resolve-inputs); no timer, no estimate, no animation

stages.title: Assemble timeline
consumes: the resolved scenes and their durations

produces.label: ordered clip timeline (clip count, total duration, first/last marks)

stages.note: Cumulative timeline arithmetic over the project's own scene order. It plans the cut; it does not cut anything.

output.durationBasis: Scene.durationSeconds as stored. A scene with no declared duration contributes 0 ms — the timeline does not invent a length.

progressAfterStage.arithmetic: 25% = (10 + 15) / 100 — weights of the 2 stage(s) that actually succeeded (resolve-inputs, assemble-timeline); no timer, no estimate, no animation

stages.title: Audio mix plan
consumes: the voice, music and SFX the project has

produces.label: audio mix plan from src/lib/mix (tracks, gains, loudness target)

stages.note: buildMix() computes the plan. The MIXDOWN itself needs an encoder, so no mixed audio file exists — the plan says so in its own record.

output.whyNoAudioFile: A mix plan is arithmetic over gains and loudness. Rendering it to an audio file needs an encoder, which this pipeline gates at the encode stage — so this stage produces no file and says so.

progressAfterStage.arithmetic: 35% = (10 + 15 + 10) / 100 — weights of the 3 stage(s) that actually succeeded (resolve-inputs, assemble-timeline, audio-mix-plan); no timer, no estimate, no animation

stages.title: Subtitle burn-in plan
consumes: the project's script text and subtitle cues

produces.label: subtitle plan from src/lib/subtitles (cue count, timing model, style)

stages.note: buildSubtitles() plans the cues and their timing model. Burning them into pixels is the encode stage's job and is gated with it.

output.timingModel: ESTIMATE: sentence timing derived from the voice director over the raw text (chars/sec model); word timing is a wpm-based estimate.
output.whyNotBurnedIn: Burning cues into pixels is an encode operation. This stage plans the cues; the encode stage is where they would reach the frame, and it is gated.

progressAfterStage.arithmetic: 45% = (10 + 15 + 10 + 10) / 100 — weights of the 4 stage(s) that actually succeeded (resolve-inputs, assemble-timeline, audio-mix-plan, subtitle-plan); no timer, no estimate, no animation

stages.title: Encode master

produces.label: master video file on disk, with bytes and SHA-256

stages.note: The first stage that must leave a file. It spawns ffmpeg with declared arguments and verifies the output exists with bytes > 0. No provider substitute is used today: the encode-provider probe is REPORTED, not gating, because the video_enhancement adapter does not take a whole timeline.

audio.statement: the clip carries an audio stream; it is re-encoded to AAC 48000 Hz stereo so the segment matches the timeline's stream layout

reasons.reason: fit the clip inside 1920×1080 without cropping (letterbox), square pixels, 30 fps, yuv420p — every number taken from the preset
an intermediate close to the source, so the delivery encode's quality is the preset's, not this step's
the preset's keyframe cadence, so the delivery encode does not have to move keyframes
the preset's H.273 code points on the intermediate as well
AAC at the preset's layout for both cases, so the concat segments agree

source.durationBasis: each clip is concatenated IN FULL: Scene.durationSeconds is not applied as a trim in this build, so the master's length is the sum of the clips' own durations, not the sum of the scenes' declared durations

measured.measuredBy: ffprobe -v error -print_format json -show_format -show_streams, read back from the file on disk

stages.title: Container / mux
consumes: the planned audio and subtitle tracks
stages.note: Muxes the container and reads it back with ffprobe to confirm the streams it claims. Needs the encode stage's file to exist — which is why it can never run before it.

output.titleWritten: Real footage, one scene — a Pixabay clip encoded by this pipeline
